entries.body:
# 1. What's Moving and What Triggered It

FACT: "125 hydrogen fuel cell trucks from three truck OEMs (Volvo Group, Scania and Hyundai) and one truck retrofitter (Hyliko) will be deployed across six EU member states/associated countries. The truck manufacturers will supply vehicles able to achieve a 400/600 km minimum range between refuels for 350/700 bar storage, respectively. 41-44 tonne articulated trucks will be included among the types of trucks to deploy, covering the longest haul road freight. The trucks will be deployed with over 20 European truck operators and operate in a wide range of conditions and day-to-day operations, across the European member states/associated countries. The trucks will operate on a developing network of hydrogen refuelling stations (HRS), designed specifically for trucks with the help of project Associated Partners, TotalEnergies, Everfuel and TEAL Mobility." *Source: H2Accelerate TRUCKS project page. https://h2accelerate.eu/trucks/

*Operational implication:* the consortium restructured from an original 150-truck, 9-country target (below) to the current 125-truck, six-country programme; this record captures the current programme as the live signal.

FACT: "Scania Pilot Partner, Hyundai Hydrogen Mobility Germany, and Hyliko have recently joined the consortium, bringing additional sector expertise and momentum to the project." *Source: H2Accelerate TRUCKS project page. https://h2accelerate.eu/trucks/

FACT: "Deploy 150 fuel cell trucks between 41 and 44 tons in 9 European countries by the end of 2029." *Source: H2Accelerate TRUCKS periodic reporting, period 1. https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101101446

FACT: "the project aims at deploying 125 hydrogen trucks in six European Member States/Associated Countries." *Source: H2Accelerate TRUCKS project page. https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101101446

*Analytical inference:* the periodic-reporting figure above (150 trucks, 9 countries, end of 2029) is the project's ORIGINAL stated objective as of its first reporting period; the current project page states the revised, smaller programme (125 trucks, six countries) quoted above. Both are recorded here so the trajectory of the signal itself is visible.

FACT: "Start date 1 February 2023 End date 31 July 2030" *Source: H2Accelerate TRUCKS project page. https://h2accelerate.eu/trucks/

FACT: "EC signature date 27 January 2023 Start date 1 February 2023" *Source: H2Accelerate TRUCKS project page. https://h2accelerate.eu/trucks/

FACT: "The funding granted by the Clean Hydrogen Partnership of €30M will enable the coordinated roll-out of heavy-duty, zero-emission vehicles fuelled by green hydrogen, bringing zero emission targets for transport closer." *Source: H2Accelerate TRUCKS project page. https://h2accelerate.eu/trucks/

FACT: "The H2Accelerate collaboration secured funding for two of their primary initiatives: the deployment of eight heavy-duty hydrogen refuelling stations under the Connecting Europe Facility and a 150 fuel cell truck project funded by the Clean Hydrogen Partnership." *Source: H2Accelerate project page. https://h2accelerate.eu/trucks/

FACT: "deployment of eight hydrogen refuelling stations in France and the Netherlands." *Source: H2Accelerate project page. https://h2accelerate.eu/trucks/

*Operational implication:* the Connecting Europe Facility award funds eight hydrogen refuelling stations located in France and the Netherlands specifically; it is not a commercial refuelling network available on arbitrary EU corridors.

# 2. Who's Driving It and What They Want

FACT: "125 hydrogen fuel cell trucks from three truck OEMs (Volvo Group, Scania and Hyundai) and one truck retrofitter (Hyliko) will be deployed across six EU member states/associated countries. The truck manufacturers will supply vehicles able to achieve a 400/600 km minimum range between refuels for 350/700 bar storage, respectively. 41-44 tonne articulated trucks will be included among the types of trucks to deploy, covering the longest haul road freight. The trucks will be deployed with over 20 European truck operators and operate in a wide range of conditions and day-to-day operations, across the European member states/associated countries. The trucks will operate on a developing network of hydrogen refuelling stations (HRS), designed specifically for trucks with the help of project Associated Partners, TotalEnergies, Everfuel and TEAL Mobility." *Source: H2Accelerate TRUCKS project page. https://h2accelerate.eu/trucks/

*Industry interpretation:* the driving parties fall into three groups: the OEM vehicle manufacturers and one retrofitter (Volvo Group, Scania, Hyundai Hydrogen Mobility Germany, Hyliko) supplying the trucks; over 20 European truck operators as the OEMs' customers deploying and operating them; and hydrogen infrastructure partners (TotalEnergies, Everfuel, TEAL Mobility) supplying refuelling capacity.

FACT: "Coordinated by SINTEF AS Norway" *Source: H2Accelerate TRUCKS project page. https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101101446

FACT: "The trucks will operate on a developing network of hydrogen refuelling stations (HRS), designed specifically for trucks with the help of project Associated Partners, TotalEnergies, Everfuel and TEAL Mobility." *Source: H2Accelerate TRUCKS project page. https://h2accelerate.eu/trucks/

FACT: "the Union submitted in October 2023 an updated nationally determined contribution (NDC) of the Union and its Member States to the UNFCCC, confirming that the Union will cut its net greenhouse gas emissions by at least 55 % by 2030 compared to 1990 levels." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610, recital citing the Union's NDC. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=OJ:L_202401610

*Analytical inference:* the European Commission's own driving interest, stated through its Fit for 55 architecture and the Union's UNFCCC nationally determined contribution, is the Union-wide 55 percent net GHG reduction target by 2030 against 1990 levels; the H2Accelerate TRUCKS programme is one demonstration project within that broader policy push, not itself a regulatory requirement.

# 3. Expected Trajectory and Conversion Triggers

FACT: "One Hydrogen Refuelling Station (HRS) every 200km on the TEN-T Core network by the end of 2030." *Source: H2Accelerate project page, citing AFIR. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/1804/oj

FACT: "REGULATION (EU) 2023/1804 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 13 September 2023 on the deployment of alternative fuels infrastructure, and repealing Directive 2014/94/EU" *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 (AFIR), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/1804/oj

FACT: "Regulation (EU) 2024/1610 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 14 May 2024 amending Regulation (EU) 2019/1242 as regards strengthening the CO 2 emission performance standards for new heavy-duty vehicles" *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=OJ:L_202401610

FACT: "New strengthened CO 2 emissions reduction targets should be set for new heavy-duty vehicles from 2030 onwards." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610, recital. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=OJ:L_202401610

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the conversion trigger for road carriers is regulatory, not this project's own timeline: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610 (amending Regulation (EU) 2019/1242) tightens fleet-average CO2 emission targets for new heavy-duty vehicles from 2030 onward, creating structural commercial pressure on carriers to transition away from diesel; the obligation runs to vehicle manufacturers and Member States, not to freight forwarders, per the captured text (Section 4).

FACT: "The final NPF document must be submitted before 1 st January 2026." *Source: H2Accelerate project page, citing AFIR National Policy Framework requirement. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/1804/oj

- 1 February 2023: H2Accelerate TRUCKS project start date (EC signature 27 January 2023).
- 13 September 2023: Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 (AFIR) adopted, setting the hydrogen-refuelling-station target this programme cites.
- 14 May 2024: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610 (amending the HDV CO2 standards) published, tightening 2030-onward fleet-average targets.
- 1 st January 2026: deadline for EU Member States' final AFIR National Policy Framework submissions.
- End of 2030: AFIR's own target of one hydrogen refuelling station every 200km on the TEN-T Core network.
- 31 July 2030: H2Accelerate TRUCKS project end date.

*Source for timeline entries: H2Accelerate TRUCKS project page (https://h2accelerate.eu/trucks/); Regulation (EU) 2023/1804, Regulation (EU) 2024/1610, EUR-Lex.*

# 4. Operational and Cost Implications If It Materializes

FACT: "The trucks to be deployed in the first stage are expected to be either 4x2 or 6x2, with up to 44 tonne capacity and long ranges of at least 600km." *Source: H2Accelerate TRUCKS project page. https://h2accelerate.eu/trucks/

*Operational implication:* the first-stage trucks are 4x2 or 6x2 configuration, up to 44-tonne capacity, with a minimum 600 km range; this is a long-haul specification, not a regional or last-mile one.

FACT: "Operators of hydrogen refuelling points shall clearly show information on the ad hoc price per kg at the publicly accessible hydrogen refuelling stations operated by them, so that that information is known to end users before they initiate a refuelling session and price comparison is facilitated." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 (AFIR). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/1804/oj

*Legal Confirmation Required:* AFIR's price-transparency and reporting obligations fall on hydrogen refuelling-point operators and EU Member States (National Policy Frameworks); none of the captured text states an obligation running to a freight forwarder procuring hydrogen-truck capacity from a carrier.

FACT: "Monitoring and reporting by manufacturers and Member States is an essential precondition for the implementation of Regulation (EU) 2019/1242." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2019/1242, recital. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019R1242

*Analytical inference:* the CO2-standards monitoring and reporting duty runs to vehicle manufacturers and Member States, not to freight forwarders or transport buyers; a workspace's exposure is commercial (carrier pricing and capacity), not a direct reporting obligation.

FACT: "This Regulation applies to any entity providing or organising freight and passenger services in the Union that calculates greenhouse gas emissions of a transport service starting or ending on the Union territory and discloses disaggregated information on those emissions to any third party for commercial or regulatory purposes." *Source: proposal COM(2023) 441 (transport GHG-emissions accounting). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=COM:2023:441:FIN

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the workspace itself falls within this proposal's scope (an entity calculating and disclosing disaggregated transport-service GHG emissions to a third party for commercial or regulatory purposes) is a fact-specific question outside this brief's scope; if it does, hydrogen-truck capacity from carriers such as those in this programme would be a data input to that disclosure, not a purchasing requirement this record grounds.

# 5. Competitive Implications

*Industry interpretation:* the OEM roster (Volvo Group as anchor, Scania, Hyundai Hydrogen Mobility Germany, and retrofitter Hyliko) represents the current hydrogen heavy-duty-truck supply base this programme is proving out; a carrier the workspace engages that is NOT among the "over 20 European truck operators" deploying these vehicles has no demonstrated participation in this specific demonstration fleet, though it may still operate hydrogen trucks through other programmes this record's pool does not cover.

FACT: "deployment of eight hydrogen refuelling stations in France and the Netherlands." *Source: H2Accelerate project page. https://h2accelerate.eu/trucks/

*Operational implication:* because the CEF-funded refuelling stations are concentrated in France and the Netherlands, a carrier's ability to offer hydrogen-truck capacity credibly on OTHER European corridors depends on infrastructure this record's pool does not confirm exists yet; competitive claims about hydrogen-truck availability on non-French/Dutch corridors should be verified against the carrier's own fleet and route data before being repeated to a client.

# 6. Client Conversation Talking Points

*Operational implication:* this is a mid-decade demonstration signal, not a live procurement option. Client-facing talking points should distinguish: (1) the H2Accelerate TRUCKS programme is a 125-truck demonstration across six EU member states/associated countries, running to 31 July 2030, not a general commercial hydrogen-trucking service; (2) the regulatory pressure driving carrier fleet transition (Regulation (EU) 2024/1610's 2030-onward CO2 targets) applies to vehicle manufacturers, not to the workspace or its clients directly; (3) AFIR's hydrogen-refuelling-station buildout (one per 200km on the TEN-T Core network by end of 2030) is the infrastructure precondition for any broader hydrogen-trucking option, and is itself a 2030-horizon target, not a present-day network.

FACT: "It will generate a comprehensive data set, which will be analysed to produce a publicly accessible report on fleet performance." *Source: H2Accelerate TRUCKS project page. https://h2accelerate.eu/trucks/

*Analytical inference:* the project's own commitment to a publicly accessible fleet-performance report is a future data point clients interested in verified hydrogen-truck performance can be pointed to once published; no publication date is stated in the captured text.

# 7. What the Workspace Should Do Now

*Analytical inference:* actions here are sequenced by lead time, not by urgency; this is a mid-decade signal, not an immediate compliance event. No sourced action deadline exists in the captured text.

GAP: no verbatim source_span in the captured text states a specific internal action deadline for the workspace; the recommended actions below follow from the dated milestones in Section 3 rather than from a source-stated action requirement.

1. Track H2Accelerate TRUCKS' own fleet-performance report (Section 6) once published, as an independent data point on real-world hydrogen-truck viability.
2. Monitor AFIR National Policy Framework submissions (due 1 st January 2026, Section 3) for early signal on which EU corridors are prioritised for hydrogen-refuelling buildout.
3. Ask carriers directly whether they participate in this or a comparable hydrogen-truck demonstration programme, rather than assuming hydrogen-truck capacity is generally available before the AFIR 2030 network target is met.

# 8. Sources

| 3 | Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 (AFIR), EUR-Lex | EU Official Journal act | https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/1804/oj |
| 4 | Regulation (EU) 2024/1610 (HDV CO2 standards amendment), EUR-Lex | EU Official Journal act | https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=OJ:L_202401610 |

metadata.what_is_it: H2Accelerate TRUCKS, a 125-hydrogen-fuel-cell-truck demonstration programme (Grant Agreement 101101446) across six EU member states/associated countries, running to 31 July 2030, alongside AFIR's hydrogen-refuelling-station buildout and the EU's tightened HDV CO2 standards.
metadata.why_matters: It signals the pace at which hydrogen heavy-duty trucking becomes commercially credible on European corridors, gated by AFIR's 2030 refuelling-network target and by the 2030-onward manufacturer CO2 standards that create the underlying carrier transition pressure.

eight CEF-funded hydrogen refuelling stations located in France and the Netherlands

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 on the deployment of alternative fuels infrastructure (AFIR), which supersedes Directive 2014/94/EU (AFID). It gives a freight-forwarding workspace a record of AFIR's Member State infrastructure-deployment targets, its own entry-into-force/application dates, and where the workspace does and does not carry a direct compliance obligation.

FACT: "OJ L 234, 22.9.2023, pp. 1–47" *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1804, EUR-Lex/Official Journal. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/1804/oj

FACT: "This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union . It shall apply from 13 April 2024." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1804, Article 26, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/1804/oj

*Analytical inference:* the regulation was published 22 September 2023 (OJ citation above) and, per its own Article 26, entered into force on the twentieth day following publication and applies from 13 April 2024.

**Convention notes.** This brief applies the regulation's provisions to the workspace's operational profile: a freight forwarder with road as a mode among others, on European trade lanes. The workspace is assessed in its freight-forwarder role, not as a Member State, infrastructure operator, or vehicle manufacturer.

**Scope limitation.** AFIR's direct compliance obligations fall on EU Member States (infrastructure deployment) and, for a small number of provisions, on infrastructure operators. **The workspace, as a freight forwarder, bears no direct compliance obligation under this regulation.** Its relevance is indirect: infrastructure deployed under AFIR determines when zero-emission road carriers become operationally viable on the corridors the workspace's carriers use.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "This Regulation establishes mandatory national targets leading to the deployment of sufficient alternative fuels infrastructure in the Union for road vehicles, trains, vessels and stationary aircraft." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1804, Article 1(1), EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/1804/oj

*Operational implication:* AFIR is a supply-side infrastructure mandate directed at Member States; it does not itself impose a vehicle-use or fuel-purchase obligation on a freight forwarder. Its relevance to the workspace runs through the road carriers it engages.

FACT: "Regulation (EU) 2024/1610 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 14 May 2024 amending Regulation (EU) 2019/1242 as regards strengthening the CO2 emission performance standards for new heavy-duty vehicles" *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610, EUR-Lex/Official Journal. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=OJ:L_202401610

FACT: "ean Parliament and of the Council of 20 June 2019 setting CO 2 emission performance standards for new heavy-du" *Source: Regulation (EU) 2019/1242, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019R1242

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Regulation (EU) 2024/1610 (amending Regulation (EU) 2019/1242) sets CO2 emission-performance standards for new heavy-duty vehicles; whether and how quickly a specific carrier the workspace engages must transition its fleet under that separate regulation is a carrier-specific, fact-specific question outside this brief's scope. AFIR is the infrastructure precondition for that transition, not its legal trigger.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*Analytical inference:* because AFIR's own compliance duties run to Member States and not to freight forwarders, there is no immediate AFIR compliance action item for the workspace. The commercial monitoring item is carrier capability on European corridors ahead of client commitments on zero-emission road transport.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 22 September 2023: Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 published in the Official Journal.
- 13 April 2024: AFIR applies, per its own Article 26 (twenty days after publication, application from this date), superseding Directive 2014/94/EU (AFID).
- 31 December 2025: publicly accessible heavy-duty electric recharging pools deployed along at least 15 % of the TEN-T road network, each pool at least 1 400 kW with at least one recharging point of at least 350 kW.
- 31 December 2027: heavy-duty electric recharging pools extended to at least 50 % of the network in each direction of travel, per the captured Article 4 provisions.
- 31 December 2035: recharging pool power output milestones reach at least 600 kW, per the captured Article 4 provisions.
- Annually, by 31 March: Member States report to the Commission on recharging deployment progress (Article 18(1)); the Commission may issue a finding and recommend corrective measures where a Member State is at risk of missing its national targets (Article 18(2), Section 6).

*Source for timeline entries: Regulation (EU) 2023/1804, EUR-Lex (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/1804/oj).*
